violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Surfaces underneath the beverage dispensing (soda fountain machine) has sticky debris and components of equipment are not being cleaned as required in the customer self service area.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. EHS instructed CFM to clean underneath the surface of the soda mountain machine in the customer self-service area.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: romaine lettuce leaves (71F) stored in metal container on top of Beverage Air 2 Dr preptop refrigerator (out of temperature control) on the prepline.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: CFM relocated romaine lettuce leaves to walk in refrigerator to cool to 41F or below.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: overfilled containers of cooked penne pasta noodles (49F) and prepared house salad (60F) tightly covered cooling for 4 hours (cooked penne pasta noodles) and 3 1/2 hours inside the walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: CFM portioned half of the cooked penne pasta noodles and prepared salad into separate containers and covered lightly to properly cool to 41F rapidly.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squeeze bottles (oil and water) on the cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS instructed CFM to place label on foo items removed from original container and not easily identifiable.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Multiple boxes (chicken) of food stored on the floor inside the walk in freezer and main kitchen (after delivery).
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS instructed CFM to relocated boxes of food to shelves inside the walk in freezer and prep counter in the main kitchen.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: metal scoop handle stored in bulk rice bin directly touching the rice and scoop/ rice spatulas stored in standing water (84F) on prep counter on the cookline.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CDI: CFM removed scoop from rice bulk bin. CFM removed scoop/ rice spatulas from standing water, washed/ rinsed/sanitized, and kept dry in between use on prep counter on the cookline.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equipment/Utensils Air Drying
violations.observation: Plastic containers were found stacked while wet after cleaning and chemical sanitization on shelves near 3 vat sink.
violations.corrective_action: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food. EHS instructed CFM to allow kitchen equipment and utensils to fully air dry before stacking for storage.

violations.observation: Grease extraction filters/ baffles in the hood system observed damaged over stovetop and fryer area on back cook line.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: EHS emailed CFM written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
